symptom: Item 2 of saingge's comment on mendixlabs/mxcli#1517 (ako/mxcli#1399): with a stored note on the first `log`, restating the flow with `@annotation(text: 'hello note', position: (200, 100), size: (150, 60))` written before `@position(300, 200)` is refused: 'the free annotations change (note "hello note" is not in the stored flow); the splice edits activities only'. With @position first, check passes
cause: Not an ordering bug: extractMicroflowAnnotations reads an @annotation before any activity annotation (@position, @caption, @color, @anchor, @excluded) as a FREE note, because describe prints free notes there (prependFreeAnnotationLines). The refusal was the defect — it claimed the note was not in the stored flow when it was, attached to the statement it was written above
fix: When an added free note's text is a note the stored flow attaches to an activity, the refusal says the note is written before @position, which makes it a free note, names the activity it is attached to, and says to write it after @position. The skill states the ordering rule
test: mdl/executor/flow_splice_note_order_pedapp_test.go TestCreateOrModify_NoteBeforePositionNamesTheOrder (check and exec both name the order; control: a genuinely new free note keeps the plain refusal without the hint). Before the fix the test failed with the reported 'is not in the stored flow'
insight: Before changing parse semantics to fix a 'wrong reading', check what describe prints: the order-dependent reading IS describe's syntax for free notes, so changing it would break every describe→exec round trip of a flow with a free note. The cheap, correct fix is a refusal that resolves the ambiguity against the stored flow and names the spelling that works
